quality.title: Feed rules every AI shopping surface enforces
quality.description: Every active product runs through one rule registry: universal checks any AI shopping agent applies, plus platform packs for Google Merchant Center's product data specification and issue codes and the OpenAI product feed spec behind ChatGPT Shopping. Every finding carries per-surface severity and a link to the official documentation.

summary.totalDetail: active products in the latest audit

issues.title: Fixes ranked by how many products they unblock
issues.empty: No rule violations across the catalog. Every listing passes both platforms' checks.

products.title: Per-product findings
products.empty: No active products yet. Sync or add products to run the quality checks.

id-duplicate.title: Duplicate product ID
id-duplicate.detail: Two or more products share the same feed ID; every listing needs a unique, stable identifier or later rows silently overwrite earlier ones.

title-gimmick-symbols.title: Gimmicky symbols in title
title-gimmick-symbols.detail: Repeated punctuation, decorative characters, or emoji read as spam to editorial checks on every surface.

title-invalid-characters.title: Invalid characters in title
title-invalid-characters.detail: Private-use or corrupted (mojibake) characters break ingestion; re-encode the text as clean UTF-8.

brand-placeholder.title: Placeholder brand value
brand-placeholder.detail: Values like "N/A" or "generic" are rejected as brands; provide the real brand or omit the attribute.

title-missing.title: Missing title
title-missing.detail: Every listing needs a plain-text title of 1–150 characters.

title-too-long.title: Title over 150 characters
title-too-long.detail: Google and ChatGPT Shopping both cap titles at 150 characters; longer titles are rejected.

title-all-caps.title: Title mostly capitalized
title-all-caps.detail: All-caps titles are flagged by automated editorial checks; capitalize only abbreviations, country codes, and currencies.

title-promo-text.title: Promotional text in title
title-promo-text.detail: Phrases like "free shipping", "sale", or "best price" belong in shipping and price attributes, not the title.

title-html.title: HTML tags in title
title-html.detail: Titles must be plain text; remove markup left over from the source platform.

title-extra-whitespace.title: Extra whitespace in title
title-extra-whitespace.detail: Leading, trailing, or repeated spaces are not allowed in titles.

title-repeated-words.title: Repeated words in title
title-repeated-words.detail: Repeating the same word reads as keyword stuffing to editorial checks.

description-missing.title: Missing description
description-missing.detail: Both platforms require a description; 500–1,000 characters describing only the product works best.

description-too-long.title: Description over 5,000 characters
description-too-long.detail: Descriptions are capped at 5,000 characters on both platforms.

description-identical-title.title: Description identical to title
description-identical-title.detail: The description must add information beyond the title.

description-promo-text.title: Promotional text in description
description-promo-text.detail: Remove promotion phrases. Price, sale, and shipping claims are checked against dedicated attributes instead.

id-too-long.title: Product ID over 50 characters
id-too-long.detail: Feed IDs are capped at 50 characters and must stay stable across syncs.

link-missing.title: Missing product URL
link-missing.detail: Every listing needs a public landing page on the verified domain.

link-invalid.title: Invalid product URL
link-invalid.detail: The landing page must be a complete http(s) URL under 2,000 characters.

link-ip-host.title: Product URL uses an IP address
link-ip-host.detail: Landing pages must use a domain name, not a raw IP address.

link-credentials.title: Credentials embedded in URL
link-credentials.detail: URLs must not embed a username or password; ChatGPT Shopping rejects them outright.

image-missing.title: Missing product image
image-missing.detail: Every listing needs at least one image; items without one are disapproved.

image-invalid-url.title: Invalid image URL
image-invalid-url.detail: Image links must be complete http(s) URLs under 2,000 characters that the platforms can crawl.

image-too-many.title: More than 10 additional images
image-too-many.detail: Google accepts up to 10 additional images per listing; extras are dropped.

price-missing.title: Missing price
price-missing.detail: Every listing needs a price; items without one are disapproved.

price-not-positive.title: Price is zero or negative
price-not-positive.detail: Prices must be greater than zero and match the landing page.

currency-invalid.title: Invalid currency code
currency-invalid.detail: Prices need a three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. USD or EUR.

sale-price-not-below.title: Compare-at price not above live price
sale-price-not-below.detail: A sale only renders when the pre-discount price exceeds the live price; otherwise the strikethrough is ignored.

brand-missing.title: Missing brand
brand-missing.detail: Branded products must carry the brand attribute; missing it limits matching into cross-retailer product clusters.

brand-too-long.title: Brand over 70 characters
brand-too-long.detail: Brand values are capped at 70 characters and must not carry promotional text.

gtin-invalid.title: Barcode is not a valid GTIN
gtin-invalid.detail: The barcode fails GTIN length or check-digit validation; use the manufacturer's GTIN-8, -12, -13, or -14.

gtin-coupon-prefix.title: GTIN uses a coupon prefix
gtin-coupon-prefix.detail: Prefixes 98–99 identify coupons and are disapproved; use the manufacturer's GTIN.

gtin-restricted-prefix.title: GTIN uses a restricted prefix
gtin-restricted-prefix.detail: Prefixes 2, 02, and 04 are reserved for restricted distribution and variable-weight goods.

gtin-missing.title: Missing GTIN
gtin-missing.detail: Without a GTIN the offer cannot join cross-retailer product clusters, which limits performance on both surfaces.

mpn-missing-without-gtin.title: No GTIN and no MPN
mpn-missing-without-gtin.detail: Provide an MPN when the product has no GTIN. ChatGPT Shopping requires one of the two, and the Google feed marks identifier_exists false without them.

googleShopping.title: Optimized listings on Google, without touching your store
googleShopping.description: ecentic layers your published listing optimizations over your existing Google product feed as attribute overrides. Your store's Google plugin keeps owning prices, stock, and the product feed. ecentic manages titles, descriptions, and diagnostics on top.

unsupported.description: Google Shopping optimization is currently available for Shopify stores. WooCommerce support is coming soon.

connect.title: Connect Google
connect.description: Sign in with the Google account that manages this store's Merchant Center. ecentic requests the Merchant Center content scope. It manages your product listings, feeds, return policies, and store contact info there, and it never touches your ads or personal data.

chooseAccount.title: Choose your Merchant Center account
chooseAccount.description: Your Google login can see several Merchant Center accounts. Pick the one the Google & YouTube channel created for this store. Accounts whose registered website doesn't match this store's domain are flagged; you can link one anyway, but it is usually the wrong choice.

waitingAccount.title: Waiting for your Merchant Center account
waitingAccount.description: Install the Google & YouTube channel in your store admin and finish its Google connection. That creates and verifies your Merchant Center account, and ecentic detects it automatically.

link.title: Link your account to ecentic
link.description: ecentic will request management access to your Merchant Center account (account {account}). This lets us attach an optimization feed and read diagnostics. You can revoke the access in Merchant Center at any time.

linkPending.title: Establishing link
linkPending.description: Your link request is being processed. This usually completes within a few minutes.

feed.title: Set up the optimization feed
feed.description: Creates ecentic's supplemental feed on your account and wires it into your primary product feed. Your store's plugin keeps owning prices, stock, and images. ecentic only layers optimized titles and descriptions on top.

disconnect.description: Removes ecentic's optimization feed and management access from your Merchant Center account. Your products and their Google listings stay; only the ecentic overrides go away. You can reconnect any time.

actions.pushed: Optimizations pushed, going live on Google
actions.description: Pushes your published listing optimizations as overrides onto the matching Google offers. Unchanged items are skipped automatically; Google re-checks policies on every override before it goes live.

diagnostics.title: Why products are disapproved or limited on Google
diagnostics.description: Reads account issues, item issues, and disapprovals straight from Merchant Center.
diagnostics.empty: No issues reported. The account and its offers are healthy.

ucp.title: Sell directly inside Google's AI surfaces
ucp.description: Google is rolling out agent-driven checkout in AI Mode and Gemini. ecentic audits your Merchant Center prerequisites and pushes the required checkout-eligibility attributes through the optimization feed it already manages.

platform.title: Payments, checkout, and order sync
platform.description: The Google Pay handler, UCP profile, checkout endpoints, and order webhooks are your commerce platform's side of the integration. For Shopify stores they ship with Shopify's own agentic checkout rails. ecentic prepares everything Merchant Center-side: readiness above, eligibility flags below.

faqSection.title: Pricing FAQ
faqSection.description: Common questions about plans, limits, and when to talk to sales.

items.question: Is there really a free plan?
items.answer: Yes. The Scan plan runs a one-time simulation of your top 10 products across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity and returns a Win Rate Report. It needs no credit card and takes about two minutes to set up.

items.question: What is the difference between Compete, Scale, and Dominate?
items.answer: Compete is for teams that want to understand where they lose: up to 100 products, daily simulations, and competitor battlecards with manual suggestions. Scale adds volume and automation: up to 1000 products, continuous simulations, and one-click or auto-published optimizations. Dominate adds the protocol layer on top of Scale (model drift alerts and UCP generation) and is the tier our Techstars deal is redeemed against. The Y Combinator deal applies to any of the three.

items.question: What is the difference between pay-as-you-go and a subscription?
items.answer: Pay-as-you-go is free to start with no card and unlocks every feature. You only pay a 3% fee on orders we can attribute to AI-agent traffic we optimize for. A subscription (Compete, Scale, or Dominate) is a flat monthly price with no performance fee, for teams that prefer predictable billing. Both run the same optimization loop; pick whichever pricing fits how you'd rather pay.

items.question: How does the pay-as-you-go performance fee work?
items.answer: On pay-as-you-go you pay a 3% fee only on orders we can attribute to AI-agent traffic we optimize for. An order counts only when it carries our attribution signal or follows a recent AI-referral visit to your store. You are never charged on your other sales, never per agent visit, and the fee is capped at $500 per month. It is free to start with no card; we only ask for a payment method once a fee is actually due. Flat subscriptions and the free Scan have no performance fee.

items.question: Can I change plans or cancel later?
items.answer: You can start on the free Scan, activate pay-as-you-go for ongoing optimization at no upfront cost, switch to a flat Compete, Scale, or Dominate subscription when you want predictable billing, and move to Enterprise once you need custom limits or security. Nothing locks you into a long contract to try the platform.

items.question: When should I talk to sales instead of self-serving?
items.answer: Book a call if you run hundreds of SKUs across multiple stores, need UCP signing or SSO, or want a custom ROI estimate for your catalog size before committing. Everything else is faster to start on the free Scan plan.

items.question: What is the EU Presence bundle?
items.answer: We partnered with EU Presence so you can go live in Europe and stay picked by AI agents in one engagement. The Compliance + AI Visibility bundle combines their GDPR representative, GPSR responsible person, and Privacy Center Plus with ecentic Scale. It is billed together with a 20% bundle discount, no minimums, and no setup fees. Book a bundle call from the pricing page to set it up.

10.title: Cookies, analytics and support chat
10.content:
Essential storage keeps you signed in, protects connection flows, remembers your consent choice and supports features you request. These technologies can operate without optional analytics consent.

Google Analytics and PostHog are optional. Analytics collection and persistent analytics identifiers begin only after you accept analytics in the cookie banner. They help measure page views and feature use. Advertising-storage, advertising-user-data and personalization consent remain denied; we do not use these tools for ad targeting.

Use **Cookie settings** in the footer to change or withdraw your choice. Withdrawal stops future optional analytics collection and clears the site’s analytics identifiers; it does not erase events previously collected while you consented. Browser settings can also remove or block cookies and local storage, although some necessary features may stop working.

The support chat service loads when you open chat. It processes the messages and contact information you provide and can use service storage to maintain that conversation. Opening chat is separate from accepting analytics. Booking a call opens the calendar provider’s service, which has its own storage and notice.

11.title: Your rights and how to request them
11.content:
Depending on the law that applies, you may request access to and a copy of your information, correction, deletion, portability, restriction, or an explanation of processing. You may object to processing based on legitimate interests and withdraw consent without affecting processing that was lawful before withdrawal. You can complain to the data protection authority in your country, place of work or the place of an alleged violation.

Email privacy@ecentic.ai from the account address where possible, describing the request and relevant store. We may ask for proportionate information to verify identity or authority; do not send an ID document unless we explain why it is needed. An authorized agent can contact us, and we may verify the authorization. We will not discriminate against you for exercising a protected right.

We aim to respond within one month and meet the deadline required by applicable law. We will explain any lawful extension, refusal or exception. Where a right to appeal applies, reply to our decision with “Privacy appeal”; we will review it and explain the outcome within the applicable period. Shopper requests concerning a merchant’s order are handled with that merchant as described in section 04.

12.title: Additional information for US residents
12.content:
State privacy rights depend on where you live, the activity involved and whether the relevant law applies to ecentic. Where the California Consumer Privacy Act applies, rights may include knowing and accessing categories or specific pieces of personal information, correction, deletion, portability, opting out of sale or sharing, and limiting qualifying use or disclosure of sensitive personal information. Other applicable state laws may include an appeal right and an opt-out from targeted advertising or certain profiling.

The categories and sources we collect are in section 02, purposes in section 03, recipients in section 06 and retention criteria in section 09. Account credentials can be sensitive personal information. We use them to provide and secure the requested service, not to infer sensitive traits. We do not sell personal information, share it for cross-context behavioral advertising, or use it for targeted advertising. There is therefore no sale or advertising-sharing activity to opt out of through this site. We do not treat a browser opt-out signal as consent to optional analytics.

Use privacy@ecentic.ai to exercise an applicable right or submit an appeal. Applicable law may exclude business contacts or processing we perform solely for a merchant; we will explain the scope in our response. Nothing in this notice limits a right the law gives you.

13.title: Children and information we do not need
13.content:
ecentic accounts are for adults acting for a business. We do not knowingly invite children under 18 to create an account or submit enquiries, and we do not knowingly collect children’s information for our own marketing. If you believe a child supplied account information, contact privacy@ecentic.ai so we can investigate and delete it as appropriate.

A merchant is responsible for the legal age, consent and product restrictions applicable to its own shoppers. Enabling an agent checkout does not waive age checks or make restricted goods eligible on an assistant, platform or payment provider.

14.title: Changes and contact
14.content:
We may update this notice when the service or our data practices change. The date at the top identifies the current version. For a material change, we will give appropriate notice by email or in the service before it takes effect where required. We will request consent when the law or a platform policy requires new consent; continued use does not replace that consent.

For questions, requests or information about processing agreements, contact privacy@ecentic.ai. The controller and registered-agent details are in section 01.

01.content:
ecentic Inc, a Delaware corporation, operates ecentic.ai ("ecentic", "we", "us"). We are the controller of personal information we use to manage our website, accounts, billing, enquiries, security and our business relationship with you.

Contact privacy@ecentic.ai for privacy questions or requests. Xhurian Shaba coordinates requests. Our Delaware registered agent is LEGALINC CORPORATE SERVICES INC., 131 Continental Drive, Suite 305, Newark, New Castle County, DE 19713, United States. This is the registered-agent address for legal service, not a staffed ecentic office or support location. Please use email for privacy requests.

For shopper information processed to provide a merchant’s checkout, the merchant is the controller and ecentic acts as its processor or service provider. Section 04 explains that relationship. A signed data processing agreement may add requirements for that processing; it does not remove an individual’s statutory rights.

This notice covers ecentic’s services and public tools. A merchant’s storefront, an AI assistant, a commerce platform or a linked third-party site has its own privacy notice.

02.title: Information we collect and its sources
02.content:
We receive information from you, people you authorize, the store and service accounts you connect, public product pages, and the browsers or systems interacting with the service:

- **Account and contact information:** name, email, business or store name, account preferences, messages, enquiries and support conversations. Passwords are hashed with scrypt, not stored as plain text. Optional sign-in providers supply the profile details authorized in their sign-in flow.
- **Catalog and store information:** domain, titles, descriptions, images and image URLs, prices, stock, SKUs, identifiers, variants and other supported product fields. Public tools also read the public URLs you submit. Avoid including personal or confidential information in a public catalog or test prompt.
- **Connection credentials:** OAuth tokens, API keys and related configuration needed to access a store or service you connect. These are distinct from the hashed ecentic agent API keys used to authenticate callers.
- **Billing information:** plan, invoice references, amounts, payment status and attribution records. Stripe or the relevant commerce platform handles payment details for your ecentic bill.
- **Technical and usage information:** request and event timestamps, page URL, referrer, browser/user-agent, device information, errors, security logs, and feature activity. Network providers necessarily receive connection information such as IP addresses. Optional analytics are controlled as explained in section 10.
- **Agent checkout information, when enabled:** products, quantities, prices and totals; shopper name, email, shipping and billing address; checkout/order identifiers and status; required store policies; and any customer-linking tokens supplied by the enabled flow. We do not ask for shoppers’ passwords or receive their card numbers in the supported checkout flow.

We do not require health records, government identification or other unrelated sensitive personal information. Account credentials and some contact or order fields can nevertheless be sensitive under applicable law; we use them only for the service, security and the purposes described here.

03.title: Why we use information
03.content:
We use information to:

- Create and authenticate accounts, connect stores, import catalogs, provide the dashboard and respond to requests.
- Compare products in simulations, explain results and generate listing fixes from the connected catalog. Store scans use ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini; separate tools may use other supported models.
- Publish a generated title and description when you choose Apply on a supported direct connection. Structured data has a separate publish action. Apply is not a preview-only step.
- Serve enabled discovery, catalog, cart and checkout functions; relay order status; measure referrals; calculate charges; and administer subscriptions.
- Diagnose failures, prevent misuse, enforce service limits, maintain records, comply with legal duties and establish or defend claims.
- Understand site and feature use with your analytics consent, and handle demo, partner and integration enquiries you submit.

Where the GDPR or UK GDPR applies, our bases are performing a contract with an individual or taking requested pre-contract steps; legitimate interests in operating and securing a business service and communicating with business representatives; compliance with legal duties; and consent for optional analytics or another activity for which we ask consent. We consider the impact on individuals when relying on legitimate interests. You can object as described in section 11.

A merchant determines the lawful basis for shopper data we process on its instructions. Do not send shopper data to catalog simulations unless you are authorized to do so and the agreed service requires it. Simulations evaluate products; they are not intended to make solely automated decisions about individuals that have legal or similarly significant effects.

04.title: Shopify, WooCommerce and agent checkout
04.content:
The Shopify app requests `read_products`, `write_products`, `read_script_tags` and `write_script_tags`. These permit catalog access and publishing, and installation of the visit-measurement script. The script sends page URL, referrer, user-agent, page type, detected assistant and an available product identifier. This merchant storefront measurement is separate from the cookie choice on ecentic.ai. The merchant is responsible for its storefront notice and any required consent.

WooCommerce uses the credentials and permissions you issue. Read-only credentials can import products; publishing requires write access. Feed imports read the supported fields from the source you supply.

Agent checkout is optional and requires a supported WooCommerce checkout connection. Shopify installation alone does not enable ecentic’s hosted checkout. The merchant remains the seller and merchant of record. We process shopper details on its documented instructions to price carts, create the order in its store, relay status to the assistant used by the shopper and support the enabled transaction. We do not use those details to advertise to shoppers or build profiles across merchants.

Card charging is handled by the merchant’s own payment gateway, using its payment setup. Your gateway’s credentials and shoppers’ card numbers are not supplied to ecentic by this supported flow. The merchant’s own terms and privacy notice govern its relationship with the shopper.

A shopper should normally make an access or deletion request to the merchant, which can ask us for assistance at privacy@ecentic.ai. We may direct a request to that merchant so the party responsible for the order can handle it.

05.title: Google Merchant Center data
05.content:
This section applies when you connect Google Merchant Center. We request `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/content` for the Merchant API operations below. Google sign-in, if chosen separately, uses the authorized name, email and profile image to identify your ecentic account.

**What we read:** the Merchant Center accounts available to your Google login, their names, IDs and registered homepages; product offers, offer IDs, feed labels, languages and supported attributes; processing and approval status, item and account issues; data source configuration and default rules; return policies and customer-service details used in checkout-readiness checks.

**What we write when you authorize the relevant feature:** an “ecentic Optimizations” supplemental data source; the primary feed’s default rule so that it reads that source first; supported product overrides in that supplemental source; and return or service-contact details you enter and save. Your primary feed continues to own prices, availability, images and links. An account-management link with ecentic’s advanced account is proposed only after your confirmation in the dashboard.

We use this data to link the right account, publish the changes you request, check the merged offers and show diagnostics. We do not sell it or use it for advertising, lending, credit decisions or unrelated purposes. Service infrastructure may process it to provide these functions; it is not disclosed to data brokers or advertisers.

Merchant Center API data is not sent to AI model providers and is not used to develop, improve or train generalized AI models. Listing generation uses the catalog connected from your store, not Google API data. Our use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including its Limited Use requirements.

Google credentials remain server-side; authenticated access checks the connected store’s ownership. The OAuth connection uses a short-lived state cookie. Disconnecting Google deletes local connection tokens and pushed-offer records and attempts to remove the supplemental source, restore the primary rule and end the management link. If a remote cleanup fails, it may need to be completed in Merchant Center. You can revoke access through [Google Account permissions](https://myaccount.google.com/permissions); that prevents further authorized API access but does not itself erase previously retained records. Section 09 covers deletion and backups.

06.title: AI providers and other recipients
06.content:
We disclose information needed for the following roles:

- **Vercel and Neon:** hosting, application execution, database storage and AI request routing.
- **Azure OpenAI and models through Vercel AI Gateway:** product catalog, questions and relevant context for simulations and listing generation. ChatGPT uses Azure when the deployment is configured; other supported routes use AI Gateway. Provider retention and abuse-monitoring policies vary. We do not promise that every route has zero retention or the same training settings. See [Gateway retention policies](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/zdr) and [training controls](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/security-and-compliance/disallow-prompt-training).
- **Sentry:** error and performance diagnostics. Default PII capture is disabled; any enabled replay masks text and media. Technical events can still contain information needed to diagnose a failure.
- **PostHog and Google Analytics:** optional website/product analytics, subject to your consent.
- **Upstash, UploadThing and Resend:** request limits/cache, uploaded-file storage, and transactional or enquiry emails.
- **Stripe and connected commerce platforms:** billing, store integrations, orders and the actions you authorize.
- **Chatwoot and Cal.com:** support conversations you open and calls you book. Their own notices also apply to their services.

Specific enabled tools may also use SerpAPI for public offer lookups, Shopify Catalog MCP, an x402 payment facilitator, or Clearbit for logo images. BabyLoveGrowth supplies editorial content, and internal tools can use ScrapeLLM. These roles do not imply that every provider receives every category of information.

We may also disclose relevant information to advisers, authorities or other parties when required by law, necessary to protect rights or safety, or as part of a business transfer subject to appropriate protection. We do not sell personal information, share it for cross-context behavioral advertising or disclose connected store data for another company’s own marketing. A list of providers and the applicable processing arrangements can be requested at privacy@ecentic.ai.

07.title: Where information is processed
07.content:
ecentic Inc is in the United States. The production database is hosted by Neon on AWS in Northern Virginia (us-east-1). Our development team is in Albania, and service providers may process information in the United States and other countries according to the selected service and account configuration. A database location is not a guarantee that every request stays in that region.

International transfers can be subject to additional requirements. Where applicable law requires a transfer mechanism, it must be covered by the relevant processing agreement and safeguards, such as an adequacy decision or approved contractual clauses. Contact privacy@ecentic.ai for the arrangements applicable to your service and to request details or copies of relevant safeguards. A country, adequacy status or provider certification is not assumed to cover every transfer merely because a provider operates there.

08.title: Security
08.content:
Our hosting and database providers protect data in transit with TLS 1.2 or later and stored database data with AES-256 encryption. Application controls include ownership checks, OAuth state validation, HMAC verification for Shopify webhooks, secure httpOnly session cookies, scrypt password hashes and SHA-256 hashes for ecentic agent API keys.

We restrict credential handling to the server and avoid sending credentials in WooCommerce request URLs. Safeguards reduce risk but cannot guarantee that every transmission or system is completely secure. Keep your own credentials private, use the minimum platform permissions needed and tell support@ecentic.ai promptly about suspected unauthorized access. Do not send passwords, full payment details or secret keys in a support message.

09.title: Retention, disconnecting and deletion
09.content:
We keep account and connected catalog records while needed to provide the service. You can request deletion through privacy@ecentic.ai. Some accounts can use the account-deletion controls in settings; billing history or a connected provider agreement may require assisted deletion first. We respond within one month, subject to a lawful extension explained to you, and confirm the outcome.

Deletion covers the account and related credentials, imported catalog, simulations and listing records except information needed for legal duties, security, disputes or outstanding transactions. Billing references and amounts are retained for the applicable accounting period; card details remain with the billing provider. A deletion request does not cancel amounts already due or authorize destruction of records we must keep.

Disconnecting a Shopify or WooCommerce store removes its local connection credentials and disables the ecentic tracking key, while retaining catalog/history until deletion is requested. Some active billing or Google connections must be handled first. Revoke keys or uninstall the app in the originating platform to revoke that platform’s grant. Google’s additional cleanup is described in section 05. Shopify’s `shop/redact` webhook also removes the shop’s data when Shopify sends the request.

Demo, partnership and integration enquiries are retained for up to 24 months after last contact and deleted sooner on request. Support, security and analytics records are retained only as needed for their purpose, subject to legal requirements and configured provider retention. The period can differ from the account’s lifetime.

Deleted information can remain in restricted backup or restore history until those copies expire. We do not use those copies for ordinary operations. If a recovery restores deleted records, the deletion must be reapplied. Ask us for the retention arrangements relevant to an agreement; we do not promise a fixed recovery or backup-purge window that has not been agreed.

02.title: What the service does
02.content:
Depending on the plan, permissions and integrations you enable, ecentic can import catalog data, compare selected products with competitors in AI simulations, generate listing content, provide structured-data and discovery tools, measure agent referrals, and serve supported catalog/cart/checkout functions through the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP).

Simulations are controlled comparisons using the selected models and inputs. They are not a live census of every assistant, an endorsement by a model provider, or a promise that a product will be recommended or bought. Scores, win rates and illustrative examples must be read with their stated scope and sample.

A supported WooCommerce connection can enable ecentic’s hosted agent checkout. Installing the Shopify app alone does not enable that checkout service. Third-party platform eligibility, geography, product policies and payment support still apply. A “Coming soon” feature is not a current service commitment.

AI and commerce providers can change models, rules, interfaces or availability. We do not control those changes. Public tools may have limits or a narrower scope than a paid account. Integration documentation and the [Privacy Policy](/privacy-policy) explain the access and processing involved.

03.title: Your account, catalog and publishing
03.content:
Keep account information accurate and credentials secure, authorize only people who should access the account, and notify us of suspected misuse. You must have the rights and permissions needed to connect a store, submit a URL or feed, supply content and instruct us to process it. Do not submit another merchant’s private credentials or confidential material without authority.

You retain your rights in your catalog, store content, customer data and other material you provide. You give us a limited right to host, copy, process and transmit it to operate and secure the features you request, including through the service providers described in the Privacy Policy. This does not give us a right to sell your private catalog or customer data.

You are responsible for the accuracy, legality, permissions and substantiation of product facts, claims, prices, stock, shipping, returns and other store policies. Generated content can contain errors. Review the source facts and choose carefully when to publish. **Apply generates and publishes a title and description on a supported direct connection; it is not a preview-only action.** Structured data is published through a separate action. Feed imports do not write changes back to the source feed.

You may use the listing fixes and reports provided for your business, subject to third-party rights. AI output may not be unique or eligible for exclusive intellectual-property protection. Nothing here transfers ownership of the platform, code, model or third-party materials to you.

04.title: Orders, payments and merchant responsibility
04.content:
For an order placed through an enabled agent checkout, you remain the seller and merchant of record. The order is created in your commerce platform under your store’s terms. You are responsible for product legality, age or other eligibility checks, taxes, pricing, availability, shipping, fulfilment, consumer notices, refunds, returns, chargebacks and customer service.

ecentic does not take title to goods and is not a party to the sale between you and the shopper. It is not your acquiring bank or payment processor. The supported payment flow uses your own payment provider and its applicable agreement. Do not expose payment secrets or card data through product fields, prompts or support messages.

Brand names and logos of assistants, commerce platforms or customers remain their owners’ property. Their appearance does not imply endorsement or a partnership. Permission to use ecentic’s name in a public customer or partner listing is not implied by these Terms.

06.title: Plans, fees and renewal
06.content:
The [pricing page](/pricing) and the billing confirmation identify the plan, limits, price and any applicable terms before activation. There are three separate products:

- **Scan:** a free, one-time analysis, without a billing row or card requirement.
- **Pay-as-you-go:** free to start, with no card required until a fee is due. It is billed only through a performance fee on qualifying AI-attributed revenue. The standard settings are 3%, a seven-day referral attribution window and a US$500 cap per calendar month, unless different settings are expressly agreed for the account. Each qualifying order’s fee is rounded to cents before summing and applying the cap. Attribution is a measurement method, not proof that AI caused a sale.
- **Flat subscription:** Compete, Scale or Dominate, with the recurring monthly charge and product limits you select. A performance fee does not apply while the account is on a flat subscription.

Flat subscriptions renew automatically each month until cancelled. Stripe handles direct billing; eligible Shopify-installed stores use Shopify’s approved billing mechanism. Pay-as-you-go uses calendar months and separate usage charges or invoices, not a performance fee added to a flat plan. You authorize the payment provider to charge amounts you approve under the selected arrangement.

Prices exclude applicable taxes unless stated otherwise. You are responsible for valid billing details and due charges. Fees are non-refundable except where the law or a written agreement requires otherwise. We will disclose a recurring price change before the renewal to which it applies, with an opportunity to cancel. Enterprise scope, targets, duration and any outcome-linked fee must be agreed in writing; an example or sales conversation is not an agreed guarantee.

07.title: Cancellation, disconnecting and deletion
07.content:
You can cancel a flat subscription through the applicable billing controls or request help at support@ecentic.ai. Cancellation normally takes effect at the end of the paid billing period, with access continuing until then. Platform-billed subscriptions must also follow that platform’s cancellation mechanism. For pay-as-you-go, use the available billing controls or contact support to stop the arrangement; fees already incurred remain payable.

Disconnecting a store, revoking a platform credential, cancelling billing and deleting an account are distinct actions. Do not assume one cancels the others. Revocation in the originating platform stops further access under that grant. Local disconnection retains imported history until deletion and may require active billing or Google connections to be handled first.

You can request account deletion at privacy@ecentic.ai or use the available settings control. Outstanding billing, provider cleanup, legal retention and backups can require an assisted process. The [Privacy Policy](/privacy-policy) explains what is deleted and retained. Export or retain records your business needs before closing the account.

After termination, you must stop using the Service. Hosted functions and store access are disabled as part of closure, but an order or charge already created remains your responsibility. Payment obligations, ownership, confidentiality, disclaimers, liability limits and dispute provisions survive where their purpose requires it.

08.title: Data protection and confidential information
08.content:
The Privacy Policy describes our handling of personal information. Where we process shopper data on your behalf, you determine the purpose and lawful basis and remain responsible for notices, permissions and instructions. We act within the requested service and any signed data processing agreement. Contact privacy@ecentic.ai to arrange a DPA or provide your proposed agreement before sharing non-public data that requires it.

Disclosure required by law is permitted, with notice where lawful and practical.

A separately signed NDA or DPA may provide more specific protection. Neither a marketing page nor these Terms establishes an unverified certification, recovery target, data-residency guarantee or custom security commitment.

09.title: Availability, changes and suspension
09.content:
We aim to operate a useful and reliable service, but do not promise uninterrupted or error-free availability or a support response time unless agreed in writing. For material changes to these Terms, we will give notice by email or in the Service before the change takes effect. Continuing to use the Service after the stated effective date accepts the revised Terms, except where law requires a different process. You can stop using and cancel the Service if you do not agree. whyListingsLose.title: Why listings struggle in AI-mediated buying.
whyListingsLose.description: Most catalog problems stem from the same gap: product data that was built for humans to browse, not for AI systems to compare.
paragraphs: AI shopping systems do not browse a page the way a human does. They compare titles, descriptions, structured attributes, price context, compatibility details, and trust signals in a compressed decision window. If one listing is clearer, more complete, and easier to compare, it wins before the shopper ever sees why.
The fix is not stuffing a page with keywords. It is making product information easier to retrieve, evaluate, and trust.

faqSection.title: Frequently asked questions
faqSection.description: Common questions from merchants researching AI product listing optimization.

items.question: What is AI product listing optimization?
items.answer: AI product listing optimization is the process of improving titles, descriptions, attributes, and supporting product context so AI shopping systems and high-intent shoppers can compare the listing more confidently.

items.question: Does listing optimization only change copy?

meta.description: Developer documentation for the REST API, MCP server, CLI, authentication, errors, rate limits and versioning.

hero.title: ecentic developer
hero.description: Everything an agent or an engineer needs to call ecentic: a versioned REST API, an MCP server, typed errors, published rate limits, and the discovery documents that let a crawler find all of it without a human in the loop.

art.alt: ASCII-art illustration of a terminal console

quickstart.title: Call ecentic in one request
quickstart.description: The public surface is unauthenticated and CORS-open. Start here, then mint a key only when you need to act on a merchant account.
quickstart.intro: Every public endpoint answers JSON, sends live rate-limit headers, and points back at its own machine-readable description through a Link header.

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.description: Public reads are open. Anything that touches a merchant account takes a bearer key.
authentication.body:
ecentic issues long-lived API keys after a human creates an account. Create the account, mint a key from the dashboard or through the authenticated MCP tool `create_api_key`, then send it as a bearer token on every protected call. The key is shown once.

Protected calls without a valid key return HTTP 401 and a `WWW-Authenticate` header naming the Protected Resource Metadata document, so an agent can re-run discovery from the failure itself rather than guessing.

- `mcp` — call MCP tools against the ecentic MCP endpoint
- `onboarding` — connect Shopify, WooCommerce, and product-feed stores

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.description: The versioned REST surface. Paths under /api/v1 are stable for the life of v1.

protocols.title: Agent protocols
protocols.description: ecentic speaks the commerce and tool protocols agents already use, and publishes a manifest for each.

reliability.title: Errors, limits, and versions
reliability.description: The three contracts an integration depends on, each documented on its own page and each machine-readable.

cards.title: Typed errors
cards.description: Every failure is application/problem+json with a stable machine-readable code and a resolution hint.

cards.title: Rate limits
cards.description: Live RateLimit headers on every response and Retry-After on a 429, so an agent can self-throttle.

cards.title: Versioning
cards.description: Version in the URL path, with Deprecation and Sunset headers before anything is removed.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.description: Claude, ChatGPT, and any MCP client can call ecentic natively.
mcp.body:
The ecentic MCP server speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP and is reachable at both `/mcp` and `/api/mcp`. Its manifest is published at the conventional well-known path and as a SEP-1649 server card.

Tools that only read (`list_plans`) work unauthenticated. Tools that change account state — creating keys, starting checkout, connecting a store — need a bearer key.

- `list_plans` — plans and their Stripe availability
- `create_api_key` — mint a long-lived agent key
- `create_checkout` — open a Stripe checkout session
- `connect_shopify`, `connect_woocommerce`, `connect_feed` — store onboarding

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: ecentic receives webhooks; it does not yet deliver them outbound.
webhooks.body:
Inbound endpoints are signature-verified and reject anything that fails the check before any handler runs. Shopify compliance webhooks verify an HMAC, Stripe verifies its own signature header, and partner endpoints verify a bearer secret.

Outbound webhooks — ecentic notifying your system when a scan finishes or a listing is republished — are not published yet. Read scan and listing results in the dashboard. The published REST API does not expose those dashboard results; use the API reference for the operations currently available. MCP requests are stateless; there is no subscription session.

cli.title: Command line
cli.description: Script ecentic without writing an HTTP client.
cli.body:
The ecentic CLI wraps the same public surface documented here — discovery, plans, skills, health, and MCP tool calls — so an agent or a developer can shell out instead of building an integration.

It reads `ECENTIC_API_KEY` from the environment for authenticated commands and prints JSON on stdout, so every command composes with `jq`.

footer.note: Every document on this page is machine-readable and reachable without a key.

meta.title: ecentic API errors
meta.description: Look up API error codes, HTTP status values and resolution hints. Responses use the RFC 9457 problem format.

hero.title: ecentic API
hero.description: Every failure on the ecentic API is a typed problem document, not an HTML page. The code is the contract: it is stable, machine-readable, and safe to branch on.

art.alt: ASCII-art illustration of a shield

shape.title: The shape of a problem
shape.description: One media type, one schema, on every 4xx and 5xx the API returns.
shape.body:
Responses carry `Content-Type: application/problem+json` — deliberately not `application/json`, because the media type is how a generic client knows the body describes a failure rather than the resource it asked for.

- `type` — URI naming the error, anchored in this page
- `code` — the stable machine-readable identifier to branch on
- `title` — short human summary
- `status` — the HTTP status, repeated in the body
- `detail` — what went wrong on this specific request
- `resolution` — what to do about it
- `instance` — the path that produced it, when known

catalogue.title: Error catalogue
catalogue.description: Codes are frozen once published. Titles and hints may be reworded; codes may not.

meta.title: ecentic API rate limits
meta.description: The ecentic public API rate-limit policy, the RateLimit headers on every response, and how agents should self-throttle.

hero.title: ecentic API
hero.description: Every public response carries the live state of your window, so an agent can pace itself instead of discovering the limit by being rejected.

art.alt: ASCII-art illustration of a balance scale

policy.title: The policy
policy.description: One fixed window on the public surface, counted per credential.
policy.body:
Requests carrying a bearer key are counted against that key; everything else is counted against the client IP, so one noisy agent cannot spend a shared address's budget.

The window is fixed, not sliding: it resets on a wall-clock boundary, and the `reset` value in the headers is the number of seconds until that boundary.

headers.title: Headers
headers.description: Both spellings are sent. Read whichever your client already understands.
headers.body: `RateLimit-Policy` is always present, because the policy is true whether or not a given request could be counted. The live counters are sent only when there is a real count behind them — an environment that cannot reach the counter omits them rather than claiming a budget nobody measured.

items.meaning: The active policy: quota and window length in seconds.
Live state: requests remaining and seconds until reset.
Requests allowed in the current window.
Requests left in the current window.
Sent only on a 429. Wait this many seconds, then retry.

exceeded.title: When you exceed it
exceeded.description: A 429 is a typed problem like any other failure.
exceeded.body: The response is `application/problem+json` with code `rate-limited`, and carries `Retry-After` alongside the rate-limit headers. Back off for the number of seconds it names rather than retrying immediately — a retry inside the same window is counted and rejected again.

meta.title: ecentic API versioning
meta.description: Read how ecentic versions its API and announces deprecations through Deprecation and Sunset headers.

hero.title: ecentic API
hero.description: The version is in the path. An integration that pins a version keeps the contract it was written against, and never loses it without warning.

art.alt: ASCII-art illustration of a calendar

strategy.title: How versions work
strategy.description: One number, in the path, changed only for a break.
strategy.body:
The current version is v1, served at `/api/v1`. Every response also echoes the version in an `API-Version` header, so a client that follows a redirect or a link can confirm what it is actually talking to.

Additive changes ship inside a version: new endpoints, new optional request fields, new fields on an existing response. Treat unknown response fields as forward compatibility, not as an error.

A change that removes a field, renames one, narrows a type, or changes the meaning of an existing value is a breaking change and ships as a new version path beside the old one — never in place.

deprecation.title: Deprecation and sunset
deprecation.description: Two standard headers, and a window long enough to act on them.
deprecation.body:
When a version is deprecated, every response from it carries a `Deprecation` header (RFC 9745). When a removal date is fixed, responses also carry a `Sunset` header (RFC 8594) naming the date the version stops answering, and a `Link` with `rel="successor-version"` pointing at the replacement.

The minimum notice between the deprecation announcement and the sunset date is 180 days. No version is removed without both headers having been served for that full window.

support.title: What is not versioned
support.description: Discovery documents track their own protocol's version instead.
support.body: The `.well-known` discovery documents are versioned by the protocol they implement, not by the ecentic API version — the UCP profile carries a UCP version, the MCP server card carries a protocol version, and so on. Reading the version from inside the document is always correct; inferring it from the ecentic API version is not.

meta.description: Connect an MCP client to ecentic. Read the transport, handshake, supported tools, authentication and error-handling reference.

hero.title: ecentic MCP
hero.description: Claude, ChatGPT, and any Model Context Protocol client can call ecentic natively over JSON-RPC 2.0. This page is the connection reference: the endpoint, the transport, the handshake, and every tool it exposes.

art.alt: ASCII-art illustration of a robot

connect.title: Connect
connect.description: One endpoint, two paths, no session to manage.
connect.body:
The server is reachable at `/mcp` and at `/api/mcp`. Both are the same handler; the bare path exists because most clients and scanners probe it first.

The transport is Streamable HTTP. Every request is a `POST` carrying JSON-RPC 2.0, and every response arrives on that same POST. ecentic opens no server-initiated stream, so a `GET` with `Accept: text/event-stream` answers `405` rather than hanging your client on a stream that will never emit.

There is no session. ecentic issues no `Mcp-Session-Id`, and `DELETE` — the session-termination verb — answers `405` for the same reason. Nothing needs to be torn down.

handshake.title: Handshake
handshake.description: Initialize, then send the initialized notification.
handshake.body:
`initialize` returns the negotiated protocol version, the server identity, its capabilities, and an `instructions` string describing what ecentic is for. If you ask for a version ecentic speaks, you get that version back; anything else falls back to the version it advertises.

The `notifications/initialized` message that follows is a JSON-RPC **notification** — it has no `id` and draws no reply. ecentic answers it with `202 Accepted` and an empty body, as the transport requires. A server that answers a notification with a JSON-RPC error breaks the handshake, so this is the one exchange worth checking first when a client will not connect.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: What the server exposes, and which calls need a key.

items.listPlans: Returns the public plan catalog with prices, billing mode, and performance-fee terms.
items.createApiKey: Mints a long-lived agent API key on the caller's account. Shown once.
items.createCheckout: Opens a Stripe checkout session for a subscription plan.
items.connectShopify: Starts the Shopify OAuth install for a shop domain.
items.connectWooCommerce: Connects a WooCommerce store with REST consumer credentials.
items.connectFeed: Connects a product feed by URL, auto-detecting XML or JSON.
items.getOnboardingStatus: Reports which onboarding steps the account has completed.

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.description: Read-only tools are open; anything touching an account takes a bearer key.
authentication.body:
Send `Authorization: Bearer ecentic_sk_…` on tool calls that change account state. A call that needs a credential and does not have one returns HTTP 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header naming the Protected Resource Metadata document, so a client can re-run discovery from the failure itself.

Keys are self-serve: create an account, then mint one from the dashboard or by calling `create_api_key` over an authenticated session. No sales contact is involved at any point.

errors.title: Errors
errors.description: Two error surfaces, and which one you are looking at.
errors.body:
A **JSON-RPC error** — an unknown method, bad params, a tool that refused — arrives as HTTP 200 with an `error` member, exactly as JSON-RPC specifies. Branch on `error.code`.

A **transport error** — a method the endpoint does not offer — arrives as an RFC 9457 problem document with `Content-Type: application/problem+json` and a machine-readable `code`. That is the same error model the REST surface uses.

The one exception is 401: it carries the JSON-RPC envelope so a client already parsing JSON-RPC does not need a second parser, plus the `WWW-Authenticate` header for discovery.

footer.note: Every claim on this page is checkable: the manifest, the server card, and the OpenAPI document all describe the same endpoint.

meta.title: ecentic API authentication
meta.description: Learn which API surfaces are public, how to obtain an agent API key, send bearer tokens and handle authentication errors.

hero.title: ecentic API
hero.description: Public discovery needs no credential at all. Anything that reads or changes a merchant account takes a bearer key you mint yourself — no sales call, no manual provisioning.

art.alt: ASCII-art illustration of a shield

open.title: What needs no key
open.body:
Every endpoint under `/api/v1` answers without an `Authorization` header, as do the well-known discovery documents, the OpenAPI document, and the MCP `list_plans` tool. An agent can learn the whole shape of the API — endpoints, plans, protocols, skills, rate limits, error codes — before anyone has created an account.

The sandbox is open too: `POST /api/v1/sandbox/simulation` returns the exact response shape of a real simulation, computed from synthetic scoring, so a client can be written and tested with no credential at all.

keys.title: Minting a key
keys.description: Two self-serve routes, both under your control.
keys.body:
Create an account, then mint a key either from the dashboard or by calling the `create_api_key` MCP tool from an authenticated session. Keys look like `ecentic_sk_…`, are long-lived, and are shown exactly once — ecentic stores only a hash, so a lost key is replaced rather than recovered.

Rotate by minting a new key and revoking the old one. Nothing about the process requires contacting a human.

sending.title: Sending a key
sending.body:
Send the key as a bearer token on every protected request. The same header works on the REST surface and on MCP tool calls.

Do not put the key in a query string: query strings end up in logs, proxies, and referrer headers, and ecentic will not read one from there.

failures.title: When it fails
failures.description: A 401 tells you where to go next.
failures.body:
A missing or invalid credential returns HTTP 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header naming the Protected Resource Metadata document (RFC 9728). Following it leads to the authorization server metadata (RFC 8414), so a client that hits a 401 can discover how to authenticate without a human reading documentation.

On the REST surface the body is an RFC 9457 problem with `code: "unauthenticated"`. On the MCP endpoint it is a JSON-RPC error with code `-32001` and a `resource_metadata` hint in `error.data`.

footer.note: Credentials are never required to evaluate ecentic — only to act on a merchant account.

execution.unresolved: Handler could not be resolved from source.

issues.autoSubmit: This form declares automatic submission. Review whether that behavior is appropriate for the action.
issues.unresolvedDefinition: Part of this definition is dynamic or indirect and could not be resolved from source.

signals.title: API evidence

coverage.title: Scan coverage

limitations.title: What this scan can tell you
limitations.staticOnly: This is a source scan. It never runs remote JavaScript, submits forms, or invokes tools. Runtime registration and execution remain unverified.
limitations.pageLimit: More linked pages were found than this scan covers. Scan a specific product, catalog, or search URL to inspect it directly.
limitations.scriptLimit: Some external scripts or referenced modules were outside the scan limit. Their tools may be missing from these results.
limitations.resourceFailures: Some pages or scripts could not be read. Findings cover only the accessible resources.
limitations.parseFailures: Some source could not be fully parsed. Dynamic or unsupported definitions may be missing.

report.nextStep: Confirm the findings in a browser that supports WebMCP and inspect its registered tools. WebMCP is evolving; these findings are not a certification or an agent visibility score.

audit.title: Review your store’s shopping tools
audit.description: Shopping workflow evidence first, followed by implementation findings. Source matches do not confirm browser availability, tool outputs, or completed purchases.
audit.checksDescription: Pass means this source check found no issue. Unknown means the evidence is insufficient. These checks are not a runtime certification.

discovery.title: Tool discovery
discovery.description: Named definitions or API evidence found in the inspected source.

metadata.title: Names and descriptions
metadata.description: Readable tool names and useful descriptions.

parameters.title: Input metadata
parameters.description: Resolvable parameter details and descriptions where provided.

implementation.title: Execution declaration
implementation.description: An identifiable handler or declarative form operation.

forms.title: Form opportunities
forms.description: Annotations and possible links to existing tools, subject to review.

coverage.title: Source coverage
coverage.description: Whether the bounded scan could read and parse its target resources.

runtime.title: Browser verification
runtime.description: Registration, tool execution, and behavior in a supported browser.

audit.findingsDescription: Review the source issues behind these shopping operations. Start with high-priority fixes; possible form integrations require checking the existing store workflow.
audit.snippetNote: Draft attributes only. Verify that the tool name and description match the form’s real operation before merging. Preserve its action, controls, validation, and consent, and review existing tools first.
audit.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the snippet and copy it manually.
audit.empty: No actionable source issues were identified. Browser verification and the scan’s coverage limits still apply.

missingToolName.title: Give this tool a clear name
missingToolName.why: A tool name could not be read from the definition. Agents need a stable identifier to select the intended operation.
missingToolName.fix: Check the complete definition and add a unique, descriptive name if it is missing. Confirm that the same name appears in the browser’s registered tools.

missingToolDescription.title: Describe what this tool does
missingToolDescription.why: A description could not be read from this definition. Without clear metadata, an agent may not know when to use the tool or what it returns.
missingToolDescription.fix: Add a description that explains the operation, expected result, and relevant constraints. If the description is generated, confirm its final value in the browser.

missingHandler.title: Check the tool’s execution handler
missingHandler.why: The inspected JavaScript definition has no identifiable execution handler. Metadata alone does not implement the operation.
missingHandler.fix: Connect the definition to its intended execute callback, or verify an existing imported handler. Keep authentication, validation, and user confirmation in the execution path.

unresolvedDefinition.title: Resolve this tool definition
unresolvedDefinition.why: Part of the definition is dynamic, indirect, or outside the inspected source. Its metadata or implementation cannot be confirmed by this scan.
unresolvedDefinition.fix: Trace the referenced variables and modules, then inspect the final registered definition in a browser with WebMCP support. Verify the name, description, inputs, and handler there.

briefDescription.title: Make the tool description more useful
briefDescription.why: The description is shorter than 40 characters and may not explain the operation well enough for an agent to choose it. This threshold is a clarity heuristic, not a WebMCP specification requirement.
briefDescription.fix: Explain when to use the tool, what it returns, and any important limitations. For a product search, describe the supported search criteria and result details.

missingParameterDescriptions.title: Explain the tool’s inputs
missingParameterDescriptions.why: Some top-level input properties lack descriptions in the inspected schema. Descriptions help agents supply the right values; they are not mandatory for every property.
missingParameterDescriptions.fix: Describe the shopping meaning of each relevant parameter: query and filters, product or variant IDs, cart-line IDs, absolute versus changed quantity, currency, or postcode. Keep required inputs aligned with the handler and provide useful examples.

duplicateToolName.title: Review overlapping tool names
duplicateToolName.why: Different source definitions share a tool name. They may conflict if registered in the same page context; reuse on separate pages is not necessarily a problem.
duplicateToolName.fix: Check where each definition registers. If both tools coexist, give distinct operations distinct names. Otherwise ensure the intended definition is the one exposed to the browser.

automaticSubmission.title: Review automatic form submission
automaticSubmission.why: This form declares automatic submission. Depending on the operation, that may bypass an expected review or confirmation step.
automaticSubmission.fix: Confirm that automatic submission is intentional and appropriate. Preserve validation and consent, and remove the automatic-submission attribute when the action should wait for user review.

unnamedFields.title: Review form fields without names
unnamedFields.why: Some form controls have no name in the inspected markup. Such controls may not map to meaningful tool inputs.
unnamedFields.fix: Add descriptive names to controls that should be submitted and exposed as inputs. Preserve labels and validation, and keep credentials, tokens, and internal fields out of tool metadata.

formOpportunity.title: Review this storefront workflow for agents
formOpportunity.why: This public form has no WebMCP form annotations in the inspected markup, and no confidently related named tool was identified. An existing JavaScript tool may still cover the workflow.
formOpportunity.fix: Review existing tools first. If this workflow would help agents, merge toolname and tooldescription into the existing form. Preserve its action, controls, validation, and consent; do not replace the form or enable automatic submission by default.

formReview.title: Review this form before adding a tool
formReview.why: The form may correspond to an existing tool or contain sensitive fields. Source inspection alone cannot determine whether another tool is needed or appropriate.
formReview.fix: Inspect any related tools and confirm how the form handles authentication, sensitive inputs, and consent. Reuse an existing operation where appropriate and keep sensitive actions under the intended user controls.

incompleteCoverage.title: Check the parts outside this scan
incompleteCoverage.why: Some pages, scripts, or definitions could not be inspected completely. The findings and tool count cover only the source that was resolved.
incompleteCoverage.fix: Review the Coverage tab, scan relevant product or search pages directly, and inspect remaining imports or protected flows in your browser. Re-run after inaccessible resources are available.

noToolEvidence.title: Confirm whether this store exposes WebMCP
noToolEvidence.why: No tool definitions or API evidence were found in the inspected source. This does not prove that the store has no WebMCP tools.
noToolEvidence.fix: Inspect the site’s registered tools in a supported browser and try a relevant product or search page. If no tools exist, start with a useful, well-defined workflow such as catalog search.

runtimeUnverified.title: Verify registration and behavior in a browser
runtimeUnverified.why: Source inspection cannot confirm that the browser registers a tool or that its handler works. This audit does not execute scripts, submit forms, or invoke tools.
runtimeUnverified.fix: Use a browser with WebMCP support to inspect registered metadata and test a safe read-only operation. Verify inputs, outputs, and error handling, and keep the intended confirmations for actions that change store state.

forms.title: Forms found in source
forms.description: Review forms in the context of real store operations. Labels are inferred from source metadata. Check existing tools before adding support; unfamiliar forms and sensitive purchase or account flows require manual review.
forms.unannotated: No WebMCP form annotations in this markup
forms.relatedNote: These tool names were found somewhere in this scan. Their availability on this page and connection to this form are unverified; confirm both before adding another integration.
forms.sensitive: Sensitive fields were detected. Review authentication, privacy, and consent before exposing this workflow to an agent.
forms.noFields: No field metadata could be read from this form.
forms.empty: No public forms were found in the inspected HTML. Forms created by JavaScript or behind sign-in may still exist.
forms.autoSubmit: This form declares automatic submission. Verify the intended user confirmation and validation before changing its WebMCP integration.

search.why: The source suggests a catalog search form. A JavaScript tool may already cover this workflow; form markup alone does not establish a missing integration.
search.fix: Review existing search tools first. Check the query field, catalog filters, pagination, and result identifiers. If a new integration is appropriate, describe the actual search inputs and preserve the form’s validation and behavior.

product.why: This appears to be a product workflow. Agents need a stable product identity and current shopping information rather than a generic form submission.
product.fix: Confirm the product or SKU identifier and the operation’s purpose. For product reads, describe price, currency, stock, and canonical URL metadata; if the form changes a cart, review cart and variant behavior instead.

variant.why: This form appears to select product options or a variant. A selected label alone may not identify the purchasable item or its current availability.
variant.fix: Check product and variant IDs, allowed option values, stock, and variant price. Preserve option validation and distinguish choosing a variant from adding it to a cart.

cart.why: This appears to change cart contents. A generic form wrapper may hide which item changes or what a quantity value means.
cart.fix: Check the variant or cart-line identifier and whether quantity is absolute or a delta. Validate stock, return updated totals with currency, and prevent unintended duplicates when requests repeat. Reuse an existing cart tool when it covers this operation.

coupon.why: This appears to apply or remove a discount. Coupon validity and the resulting price depend on the current cart and store rules.
coupon.fix: Validate codes on the server against the correct cart. Explain acceptance and rejection, return updated discounts and totals with currency, and preserve the store’s existing coupon restrictions.

shipping.why: This appears to collect shipping information or request an estimate. An estimate is different from confirming delivery details or placing an order.
shipping.fix: Use only the country or postcode data needed for an estimate. Describe returned methods, costs, currency, and estimate limitations. Preserve address validation and checkout consent; do not expose customer details unnecessarily.

checkout.why: This form appears to enter checkout or purchase confirmation. Exposing it as a generic submit tool could obscure a consequential step.
checkout.fix: Review this flow manually. Distinguish navigation to checkout from placing an order, preserve cart state and validation, and retain the intended authentication, payment handoff, and explicit purchase confirmation.

orderTracking.why: This appears to concern an existing order. Order-history navigation alone does not mean an agent can read authorized order data.
orderTracking.fix: Review the flow manually. Require the correct authentication and ownership checks before returning status, tracking, or customer data. Scope identifiers to the current buyer and preserve any secure user handoff.

returns.why: This appears to involve a return or another post-purchase operation. Reading a returns policy and creating a return are different capabilities.
returns.fix: Review this flow manually. Verify order ownership, item eligibility, and store policy, limit personal data, and require the intended confirmation before initiating a return, refund, or order change.

newsletter.why: This appears to be a marketing subscription form, not a core product-search or cart operation. It may already have a separate integration.
newsletter.fix: Keep marketing consent explicit and separate from shopping actions. Review existing integrations before considering an agent tool; do not enroll a buyer as a side effect of search, cart updates, or checkout.

contact.why: This appears to be a contact or support form. Its presence does not by itself justify a new shopping tool.
contact.fix: Confirm the support use case and existing integrations. Preserve validation, spam protection, and consent, and do not expose a generic submission operation without a clear merchant purpose.

account.why: This appears to handle account access or customer details. Authentication must not be replaced by a generic form tool.
account.fix: Review this flow manually. Keep authentication and account ownership checks in the existing secure flow, protect passwords and tokens, and use an explicit user handoff where sign-in is required.

other.why: The source did not establish a specific shopping purpose for this form. A missing annotation is not enough to recommend a new tool.
other.fix: Identify the merchant workflow and inspect existing tools before changing anything. This scan alone does not recommend wrapping an unknown form or automating its submission.

commerce.title: Shopping workflows
commerce.description: Source evidence across eight store operations. Expand a workflow for source links and merchant checks. This audit does not call the tools or test their outputs.

unconfirmed.title: Storefront context is unconfirmed
unconfirmed.description: This page did not provide enough product, catalog, cart, or commerce-tool evidence. Try a public product or collection URL. The workflows below are inspection guidance, not a list of missing store features.

commerce.guidance: What to verify for your store
commerce.notObserved: Not observed means no matching evidence was found within this scan. It is not a defect or proof that a shopping capability is absent.
commerce.evidenceNote: Matches are inferred from source names, descriptions, fields, and URLs. A related tool may be registered on another page; availability, outputs, and connection to these forms remain unverified.

catalogSearch.title: Catalog search
catalogSearch.purpose: Find relevant products by query and shopping filters.
catalogSearch.guidance: Review query, category, price, availability, and pagination inputs. Search results should identify each product and make its price, currency, and availability clear.

productDetails.title: Product details
productDetails.purpose: Read the information an agent needs to compare a product.
productDetails.guidance: Check product identifiers, canonical URLs, descriptions, current prices, currency, and stock metadata. A link to a product page is not proof that a tool returns those details.

variants.title: Variant selection
variants.purpose: Match size, color, and other options to a purchasable variant.
variants.guidance: Check product and variant IDs, allowed option values, current stock, and variant pricing. Confirm how invalid or unavailable combinations are reported before changing a cart.

cartRead.title: Cart contents
cartRead.purpose: Inspect the buyer’s current items and totals.
cartRead.guidance: Review whether the operation returns cart and line identifiers, selected variants, quantities, discounts, totals, and currency. Opening the cart page does not demonstrate that these values can be read.

cartUpdate.title: Cart changes
cartUpdate.purpose: Add, remove, or update items without unintended duplicates.
cartUpdate.guidance: Check whether quantity means an absolute amount or a change. Validate variant and line IDs, stock, coupon codes, recalculated totals, and currency; confirm how repeated requests are handled.

checkout.title: Checkout handoff
checkout.purpose: Move the buyer into the intended checkout and confirmation flow.
checkout.guidance: Distinguish opening checkout from placing an order. Review cart continuity, validation, authentication where required, and the manual handoff for payment and purchase confirmation.

policies.title: Shipping and returns policies
policies.purpose: Explain delivery, returns, and the terms that affect a purchase.
policies.guidance: Review accessible shipping and returns terms. Shipping estimates need appropriate country or postcode inputs, costs and currency; a policy page alone does not establish live quote availability.

orders.title: Orders and aftercare
orders.purpose: Support authorized order questions and post-purchase requests.
orders.guidance: Opening order history is not the same as reading order data. Verify authentication and ownership for tracking or returns, limit personal data, and preserve confirmation before initiating a return or changing an order.
