faq.title: Understand your audit.
faq.description: A store audit connects WebMCP source findings to the shopping journey. Browser verification confirms whether the tools expose the expected data and behavior.

items.question: What does WebMCP add to a store?
items.answer: WebMCP lets a website describe tools for browser agents, such as product search or cart actions. The draft includes JavaScript registration and HTML form declarations. A tool is available only when the website and the browser expose it successfully.

items.question: How does the scanner find WebMCP?
items.answer: It reads the entered public page, up to two linked catalog, product, or search pages, and at most twelve external scripts or modules, including CDN resources. It follows explicit script references and imports, including dynamic module URLs. It looks for form attributes such as toolname and tooldescription, and JavaScript references to document.modelContext or the earlier navigator.modelContext API. It does not execute the code.

items.question: Does a finding mean an agent can use the tool?
items.answer: No. Source may contain disabled code, feature checks, or definitions that fail at runtime. This scanner does not execute JavaScript or call any tool. Confirm registration in a browser that supports the API.

items.question: What should I do if nothing is found?
items.answer: Try a product, catalog, or search page directly. Tools can be registered after JavaScript runs, loaded by other scripts, or exposed only after sign-in. No evidence in this scan does not prove your store has no WebMCP support.

items.question: What does ecentic do?
items.answer: ecentic is one layer between your catalog and the AI assistants that sell it. It simulates how ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini compare products, helps improve the data they read, and supports agent checkout on WooCommerce.

items.question: Which AI assistants does it cover?
items.answer: Store simulations run on ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. Shopify visit tracking recognises supported AI referral signals, including ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini and Copilot. Checkout depends on your store setup and the shopping platform’s eligibility. Each AI channel page shows the current status.

items.question: Does ecentic change our store without asking?
items.answer: Listing changes require your chosen Apply action, which generates and publishes a title and description. Structured data and Merchant Center sync use separate controls. Connecting Shopify also installs the visit-tracking script. Importing product content does not rewrite it.

items.question: Does it work with our platform?
items.answer: Shopify and WooCommerce connect directly. Other platforms can import a supported XML or JSON product feed or a CSV. Feed support depends on the export structure and mapped fields; feed imports do not write back to the original platform.

items.question: Do you need access to our systems for a pilot?
items.answer: A pilot can start from an accessible public catalog or a supported product feed. We agree the scope with you before any system integration or store-write access is required.

items.question: How is our data handled?
items.answer: The security page describes current catalog access, tracking and AI-provider handling. Review our privacy policy and the providers used by the product, then confirm data processing, deployment and contracting requirements with us before a pilot.

items.question: Is this SEO?
items.answer: ecentic focuses on the product data and checkout that AI shopping assistants use to compare and buy. The work can overlap with structured-data and catalog quality practices, but its measurements are simulations, detected AI referrals and checkout checks, rather than search rankings.

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: The store check is free with an account. Single stores can choose a monthly plan or pay-as-you-go. The performance-fee attribution rules and limits are explained on Pricing; attribution does not prove incremental sales. Enterprise pilots are scoped with you.

sections.title: Requirements and limits
paragraphs: Approve Shopify OAuth permissions: read_products, write_products, write_script_tags and read_script_tags. No Shopify Plus requirement is enforced by this connection.

The connection uses Shopify Admin API access and its rate limits. The sync is bounded by page count; no additional fixed requests-per-minute allowance is promised. Public-only catalog imports cannot publish changes.

faqs.question: Does ecentic change product content without asking?
faqs.answer: No. Listing content changes require Apply or an explicit bulk action. Structured data is published separately. Connecting does install the tracking script, so connection is not a promise of zero changes to the store configuration.

faqs.question: Why use ecentic if Shopify already distributes my catalog?
faqs.answer: Catalog distribution and product quality are different jobs. ecentic compares selected listings with competitors and lets you publish changes to the data you control. It does not guarantee recommendations in any channel.

faqs.question: Can I connect Google Merchant Center?
faqs.answer: Yes, for Shopify stores. Use the separate Google sync control to send published title and description overrides plus selected checkout attributes. Clicking Apply on a listing does not automatically sync Google.

faqs.question: How does the tracking script load?
faqs.answer: Shopify installs it with its onload event. The script detects supported referral or agent signals and sends a small beacon to ecentic. We have not measured a universal performance impact and do not claim zero overhead.

sections.title: A catalog and checkout agents can use

items.title: Simulate
items.body: Compare your selected products with named competitors on ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

items.title: Fix and publish
items.body: Apply publishes a revised name and description through the WooCommerce REST API. Structured data is a separate action, rendered by the plugin.

items.title: Agent checkout
items.body: Let compatible agents search products, price a real cart and create a WooCommerce order. Your payment gateway handles the payment.

sections.title: You control agent checkout
paragraphs: The plugin publishes a discovery profile at a standard address on your own domain. Cart quotes use WooCommerce stock, tax, shipping and coupon rules. Orders are tagged as agent orders; you remain the seller of record.
Switch checkout on or off, configure an agent allow-list, require signed requests and set rate limits. A blank allow-list permits all supported agents. Signature requirements are optional settings.

By default, the agent creates an unpaid order and the buyer pays through your checkout link. Server-side Stripe payments are optional, off by default and require the WooCommerce Stripe Gateway. Payment secrets stay on your server.

sections.title: What ecentic reads and writes
sections.description: The plugin and approved REST credentials provide the catalog and order operations needed for your chosen features.

sections.title: Requirements and limits
paragraphs: The published plugin requires WordPress 6.0+, WooCommerce 7.0+ and PHP 8.0+. Connect from wp-admin, or supply WooCommerce REST keys; publishing requires read/write access.
Catalog sync reads at most 20 pages of 100 products: up to 2,000 records per run. The free onboarding scan selects up to 10 products.

Hosted agent endpoints default to 120 requests per minute, per store and client identity. The merchant can configure the limit. Agent checkout needs the plugin; REST catalog keys alone do not install the checkout surface.
AI visit tracking and ecentic’s Merchant Center sync are not available for WooCommerce today.

faqs.question: Is the plugin free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Install it free from WordPress.org. ecentic plans apply to simulations and listing features; see Pricing for current terms.

faqs.question: Does ecentic take the payment?
faqs.answer: Your existing gateway takes payment and the order belongs to you. The default flow hands the buyer to your payment page. Optional server-side Stripe payment requires the gateway and its setting to be enabled.

faqs.question: Do you track AI visits on WooCommerce?
faqs.answer: Not yet. AI visit tracking runs on Shopify today.

faqs.question: Can we turn agent checkout off?
faqs.answer: Yes. Disable it from the plugin settings. You can also restrict agents, require signatures or revoke the connection credentials.

faqs.question: Do we need to change our theme or copy API keys?
faqs.answer: The plugin provides the discovery and bridge features. Approve its connection in wp-admin without copying keys, or use read/write REST keys for catalog publishing. Test any theme or payment setup on staging first.

sections.title: What ecentic reads and writes

sections.title: Requirements and limits
paragraphs: A connected Shopify store and a Merchant Center account you can authorize. The current ecentic connection does not support WooCommerce.
Google OAuth scope: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/content. Select the merchant account and complete the account-linking steps shown in the connection flow.

Matching relies on the Shopify product identity and the Merchant Center offer. Google’s diagnostics and processing determine whether each change is accepted. No fixed sync-completion time is guaranteed.
Published listing changes are sent only when you run the sync action. Background maintenance checks existing overrides and account links; it does not automatically send newly published listing fixes.

faqs.question: Will this overwrite our main feed?
faqs.answer: The main data source is retained. ecentic creates a supplemental source and updates its priority in the primary source’s rules. The selected supplemental attributes can therefore replace the effective values Google uses for those fields.

faqs.question: Is it available for WooCommerce?
faqs.answer: Not yet. ecentic’s Merchant Center integration supports Shopify today.

faqs.question: Does this get us into Google’s checkout program?
faqs.answer: No. Google decides eligibility and approval. ecentic prepares data, checks settings and helps test readiness; enrollment is your separate step.

faqs.question: Does Apply automatically update Google?
faqs.answer: No. Apply publishes the selected store listing change. Use the separate Merchant Center sync action to send published overrides to Google.

security.title: Security and trust
security.description: How ecentic handles your catalog, your store access and your customers’ data. We update this page as we grow, and the date below changes when we do.

sections.title: Last updated 12 November 2026
sections.description: This page describes controls in the current product. Confirm the deployment, processing locations and contractual requirements for your account before sharing non-public data.

sections.title: How we touch your store
paragraphs: Importing product content does not rewrite it. Apply generates and publishes a title and description on a directly connected Shopify or WooCommerce store. Structured data uses a separate publish action. Connecting Shopify also installs the visit-tracking script.
If you connect Merchant Center for Shopify, ecentic adds a supplemental data source for published fixes and checkout attributes. It does not replace your main feed.

On Shopify, a storefront script records visits when it detects an AI assistant referrer or a known agent user-agent. It sends the full page URL, browser user-agent, referrer, page type, detected agent and detection method, and an available product identifier. The record includes the store and the time received.
This browser script observes visits that run JavaScript. It does not measure every crawler request or establish that a later order came from the same shopper.

Shopify access uses the Shopify Admin API and the permissions shown on the install screen. You can uninstall at any time. WooCommerce connects through the ecentic plugin or REST API keys that you create and can revoke.

When you enable agent checkout on WooCommerce, the checkout bridge creates real orders in your store. Your gateway takes payment and you remain merchant of record. Agent checkout supports signed requests, agent allow-lists and configurable rate limits; enforcement follows your store settings.
Enterprise pilots can start from public pages and product data, without access to your systems.

sections.title: AI models and your data
paragraphs: The product catalog you connect is sent to AI providers to compare listings and write fixes. Store scans use ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. GPT also generates listing rewrites and structured data. Perplexity is used in the separate comparison and discovery tools, not store scans.
GPT runs through Azure OpenAI when an Azure deployment is configured. Anthropic, Google and Perplexity requests use the Vercel AI Gateway; GPT can use that gateway as a fallback.
Data read from a connected Google Merchant Center account is kept separate from the store catalog used for AI work, as described in the privacy policy.
Provider retention policies apply to requests. Some providers retain requests for abuse monitoring; we do not promise zero retention across every model route.

sections.title: Why we started
paragraphs: Whether people search Google, shop on Amazon or ask a chatbot, AI now answers with a product. Most stores have no idea how to be that product. They can’t see the decision, they can’t see why they lost it, and their analytics count the traffic as direct. We started ecentic to show stores that decision and help them fix it, product by product.

overview.title: Everything a store needs to sell through AI.
overview.description: Five steps, in order. Connect your catalog, see how AI models compare it, improve the data they read, test the path to checkout and track what you can observe. You choose what to publish and when to rescan.

sections.title: Your catalog, in one place. Product content stays in your control.

items.body: Check AI crawler rules in robots.txt, Product JSON-LD in sampled page HTML, product identifiers, content depth and generated-feed eligibility. Pages that cannot be fetched are reported as warnings. The audit does not execute a browser or certify that no bot wall exists.

faqs.answer: See the Pricing page. Enterprise pilots are scoped on a call.

faqs.question: Does ecentic publish anything on its own?
faqs.answer: The current listing flow requires an explicit Apply action, including any bulk action you choose. Structured data and Merchant Center sync have separate controls.

faqs.question: What exactly gets written?
faqs.answer: Listing Apply writes the title and description. Structured data is published separately. Shopify stores can send published fixes to Merchant Center with a separate sync. Prices and stock are not rewritten by the listing action.

faqs.question: Is the lift you show measured?
faqs.answer: It is an estimate per fix. A new scan lets you compare a later set of simulated decisions. It is not a measurement of added sales.

faqs.question: Will it change our brand voice?
faqs.answer: The rewrite starts from existing product facts. Apply generates and publishes it, so choose that action only when you are ready for the listing to change. There is no generated-copy preview step today.

sections.title: Three ways to start.

items.title: Audit
items.body: 4 weeks, fixed fee. A baseline of how assistants answer agreed questions in one category, the data issues worth investigating and a prioritized fix list for your team.

items.title: Pilot
items.body: 6 weeks, one market, one category. Baseline at week 0, agreed data changes and the same questions at week 6. Any outcome-linked fee and target are agreed in advance.

items.title: Design study
items.body: 3 months, with scopes that can run up to 6. For checkout or booking questions that need more than a fix list. The scope can include a prototype with dummy data and agreed readouts.

sections.note: Fees depend on scope and are agreed on the first call. These are service engagements; the pilot readout follows the method agreed with your team.

items.title: Week 0: baseline
items.body: We agree the questions at kickoff and run each one several times on every assistant, before changing data.

items.title: Weeks 1 to 5: fix
items.body: Work on the agreed category and test checkout where it applies. Public-data work is handed to your team; direct changes need explicit authorization.

items.title: Week 6 · Re-run
items.body: Repeat the agreed questions with the same assistants and number of runs. Document model or access changes.

items.title: Readout
items.body: Review what moved, the limits of the method and proposed next steps. You decide whether to continue.

faqs.question: Can AI buy alcohol for a shopper?
faqs.answer: It depends on the channel, location and age-verification flow. ecentic does not grant permission to sell a restricted product or guarantee a compliant automated purchase.

faqs.question: Do we need a GTIN on every bottle?
faqs.answer: Use the correct manufacturer-assigned identifier where one exists. Do not invent a GTIN for a limited release or reuse another product’s identifier.

faqs.question: What about limited releases with no stock feed?
faqs.answer: Keep the public listing and any supported import accurate. The importer does not create a live inventory connector for an unsupported platform.

faqs.question: How do age checks work with agent checkout?
faqs.answer: Validate your store’s exact requirements on a staging flow. The current checkout implementation does not establish a universal alcohol age-verification solution.

faqs.question: Does this work for thousands of bottles?
faqs.answer: Start with a supported catalog import and one category. Self-serve plan limits stay in place; larger scopes are agreed for an enterprise pilot.

meta.title: Selling electronics through AI assistants
meta.description: Make model numbers, battery life, compatibility, connections and warranty clear. Compare electronics listings with named competitors.

consumer-electronics.title: Selling electronics when AI compares the spec sheet.
consumer-electronics.description: Electronics questions are often about battery life, compatibility or ports. Give each model and variant clear identifiers and source specifications so a comparison does not depend on a product name alone.
questions: noise-canceling earbuds with the longest battery under $200
Laptop for video editing with 32 GB of RAM
Robot vacuum that works with Google Home

faqs.question: Our model numbers differ by retailer. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can make matching ambiguous. Use the correct model and variant identifiers, and make any genuine retailer-specific configuration explicit.

faqs.question: Do we need GTINs?
faqs.answer: Provide the correct assigned GTIN where available. Never generate one or borrow it from a similar product.

faqs.question: Will a model compare on price alone?
faqs.answer: The question and available facts affect the comparison. State battery, compatibility and other relevant specifications so the model can inspect them.

faqs.question: How should refurbished products appear?
faqs.answer: State refurbished condition, the actual configuration, price and warranty terms. Do not present them as new.

faqs.question: Our dimensions are only in a drawing. Is that a problem?

faqs.question: How should made-to-order lead times appear?

faqs.question: We offer one sofa in 20 fabrics. How should it look?
faqs.answer: Identify each variant’s fabric, color, price and availability. Use correct dimensions if a variant changes them.

faqs.question: Can AI buy a sofa for someone?
faqs.answer: It depends on the channel and supported checkout flow. Test delivery requirements and payment handoffs on a staging store before enabling agent orders.

sections.title: How this assistant shops
sections.description: Google’s shopping experiences use Merchant Center catalog data. Universal Cart launched in the US on 15 October 2026, with options to continue to a merchant’s cart or use Google Pay where checkout is enabled. The merchant remains the seller of record.

sections.description: Google lists native checkout for select merchants with eligible products in the US, Canada and Australia. Its Merchant Center integration hub is rolling out in the US first; Canada and Australia are expected early next year. Merchants must complete Google’s technical validation and approval steps.

capabilities.simulate: Gemini compares selected products with named competitors in ecentic’s store scans.

faqs.question: Do we need Merchant Center for Google’s checkout?
faqs.answer: Yes. The documented merchant route runs through Merchant Center. Your account, products and checkout integration must meet Google’s eligibility requirements.

faqs.question: Can ecentic join Google’s checkout program for us?
faqs.answer: No. ecentic helps prepare and test data and settings. The application, validation and approval remain between your business and Google.

faqs.question: Does Merchant Center sync work on WooCommerce?
faqs.answer: Not yet. ecentic’s Merchant Center connection is available for Shopify stores today.

faqs.question: Is there really a free plan?
faqs.answer: Yes. The free store check runs a one-time simulation of your top 10 products across ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini and returns a Win Rate Report. No credit card is required.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Compete, Scale, and Dominate?
faqs.answer: Compete covers up to 100 products with competitor comparisons and manual optimization suggestions. Scale covers up to 1,000 products with listing suggestions you can review and publish using Apply. Dominate includes Scale and is the plan tied to the Techstars offer. The Y Combinator offer can apply to any flat subscription. Simulations are on demand; the product does not promise a scheduled cadence.

faqs.question: What is the difference between pay-as-you-go and a subscription?
faqs.answer: Pay-as-you-go has no upfront fee and uses a standard 3% performance fee, capped at $500 a month, under the attribution rules below. Compete, Scale and Dominate charge a flat monthly price with no performance fee. Choose the billing model that fits your team.

faqs.question: How does the pay-as-you-go performance fee work?
faqs.answer: An order counts if it carries an explicit AI attribution signal, or if any AI-referred visit reached your store in the preceding 7 days. This is a store-level window, not individual shopper attribution. The standard fee is 3% of qualifying orders, capped at $500 per calendar month. Visits have no fee. A payment method is only requested when a fee is due. The free check and flat subscriptions carry no performance fee.

faqs.question: Can I change plans or cancel later?
faqs.answer: Yes. Start with the free check, activate pay-as-you-go, or choose a flat subscription. Plans are month to month and you can cancel. Talk to us to scope an enterprise pilot before agreeing its terms.

faqs.question: When should I talk to sales instead of self-serving?
faqs.answer: When you run several stores or brands, have thousands of products, need a security review, or want a pilot with targets agreed in writing.

faqs.question: What is the EU Presence bundle?
faqs.answer: The bundle combines EU Presence’s GDPR representative, GPSR responsible person and Privacy Center Plus with ecentic Dominate. The existing bundle offers a 20% discount, with no minimums and no setup fees. Use the bundle call link to discuss it.

faqs.question: What happens to our data if we leave?
faqs.answer: Request deletion at privacy@ecentic.ai. We respond within one month and confirm once data has been deleted from our systems. Billing records are retained where required by law; backup copies are removed when they expire. See the Privacy policy for scope and disconnect controls.

faqs.question: Is anything billed that we did not ask for?
faqs.answer: No plan is billed without activation. Plans are month to month. Under the standard pay-as-you-go terms, a 3% fee applies to an order with an explicit AI attribution signal or an order within 7 days of an AI-referred visit to your store, up to $500 per calendar month. The referral window covers the store, not an identified shopper. Flat subscriptions have no performance fee.

faqs.question: Do you sign a DPA?
faqs.answer: Yes. A DPA is arranged on request before personal data is shared, and we can sign yours. The contracting entity and signatory are confirmed in the agreement.

meta.title: About ecentic
meta.description: ecentic is an agent-commerce optimization platform that simulates how AI shopping agents compare your products with competitors, diagnoses why you win or lose, and rewrites the listings so those agents pick you, for Shopify and WooCommerce merchants.

hero.description: ecentic is an agent-commerce optimization platform that simulates how AI shopping agents compare your products with competitors, diagnoses why you win or lose, and rewrites the listings so those agents pick you, for Shopify and WooCommerce merchants.

does.title: What ecentic does
does.description: Four jobs, in the order a merchant actually needs them. Each one produces a result you can read, not a score with no next step.

items.title: Simulate shopping agents
items.body: ecentic runs ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity against your products and the competitors you choose. Each model scores both listings and picks a winner. You get a win rate, not a generic content grade.

items.title: Diagnose the loss
items.body: Every simulation keeps the agent's reasoning: which attributes it read, where the competitor was more complete, and which model favored which side. Battlecards turn that into a per-product comparison. The gap is visible instead of guessed.

items.title: Optimize the listing
items.body: The product rewrites titles, descriptions, and structured attributes from the losses it just measured. You approve the change in one click, or Scale, Dominate, and pay-as-you-go can publish it back to Shopify or WooCommerce. A later simulation measures whether the win rate moved.

items.title: Make the catalog agent-readable
items.body: A Universal Commerce Protocol profile gives agents a structured way to discover the store. ecentic generates that profile from the catalog you already connected. Agents that skip marketing HTML still have something precise to read.

different.title: What makes ecentic different
different.description: The tools merchants already shortlist solve a neighboring job. The difference is which decision ecentic is built to change.

items.title: It judges the agent decision, not the word count
items.body: Hypotenuse AI drafts descriptions and bullets across a catalog too large to write by hand. ecentic asks which listing an agent selects when two products are compared. If the copy already reads well and the agent still picks the competitor, a generator will not show you why.

items.title: It sees the competitor
items.body: Shopify Magic drafts inside the admin you already use, and it only ever sees your store. ecentic places your listing next to a competitor's and asks the same models a shopper would. The diagnosis is the gap between the two, not a rewrite of your page in isolation.

items.title: The choice happens before your theme
items.body: Nosto changes what a returning visitor sees on your site: recommendations, segments, and merchandising rules. Agent shopping often ends before anyone lands on that theme. ecentic works on the listing the agent reads while it is still choosing.

items.title: A lean team can start the same day
items.body: Bloomreach runs search, merchandising, and campaign data as one stack, and that implementation outruns the problem a lean team has today. ecentic starts with a free scan of 10 products. There is no implementation project before the first result.

items.title: The terms are month to month
items.body: Every paid plan is month-to-month, with no minimums and no setup fee. Pay-as-you-go stays free until an AI-attributed order, then takes 3% of that order, capped at $500 a month. Flat plans are Compete at $14.90, Scale at $44.90, and Dominate at $149, with no performance fee.

stories.title: How ecentic started
stories.body: Shopping agents read structured product data. They do not scroll a theme or trust a brand paragraph. ECENTIC SH.P.K. was founded in Tirana on 4 April 2026 to close that gap for Shopify and WooCommerce merchants.

stories.title: Who is on the team
stories.body: Three founders, engineering in Tirana, and zennit as the studio behind the product. Self-serve customers work in the product itself. Enterprise accounts get a named customer success manager, quarterly reviews, and a direct engineering escalation path.

We do not publish a response-time number; Enterprise accounts have a named customer success manager and a direct engineering escalation path.

items.title: Who you work with
items.body: On the free scan, pay-as-you-go, Compete, Scale, and Dominate, you work in the product: the scan, the battlecards, and the optimization queue. Enterprise adds a named customer success manager. There is no agency team between you and the listing.

items.title: Onboarding
items.body: Connect Shopify or WooCommerce, choose the products, add competitor listings, and run the scan. The free scan covers your top 10 products across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity. No credit card is required to start.

items.title: Turnaround
items.body: A free scan returns in about two minutes. Listing rewrites then wait in a queue you approve in one click, or they publish automatically on Scale, Dominate, and pay-as-you-go. Compete resimulates daily. Scale and Dominate run continuously.

items.question: What is ecentic?
items.answer: ecentic is an agent-commerce optimization platform for Shopify and WooCommerce merchants. It simulates how ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity compare your products with competitors, shows why you win or lose, and rewrites the listing from that evidence.

items.question: Who founded ecentic?

items.question: How much does ecentic cost, and can I cancel?
items.answer: The scan is free. Pay-as-you-go is 3% of AI-attributed orders, capped at $500 a month, with no card until a fee is due. Compete is $14.90, Scale is $44.90, and Dominate is $149 a month, with no performance fee. Plans are month-to-month and you can cancel anytime.

items.question: How is ecentic different from Shopify Magic or a copy tool?
items.answer: Shopify Magic drafts inside your admin and only sees your store. Hypotenuse AI drafts catalog copy at scale. ecentic compares your listing with a competitor's, asks the shopping agents which one they pick, and rewrites from that result.

checks.title: Know what each check tells you.
checks.description: Seven checks separate source findings, improvement opportunities, and the evidence that still needs a browser.
checks.workflowsNote: These eight workflows are useful review areas. A store does not need to expose every one through WebMCP.

items.discovery: Named declarations are recovered from HTML forms or registration code. An API reference alone leaves the available tool inventory unresolved.
items.metadata: Review tool names, descriptions, and possible duplicate names on the same page. Short descriptions are a quality suggestion, not a protocol failure.
items.parameters: Inspect recoverable input names, types, descriptions, and required state. A parameterless tool may omit its input schema; dynamic schemas can remain unresolved.
items.implementation: The source can show a declared handler or form operation. The scanner does not run the handler, submit the form, or confirm its behavior.
items.forms: Public forms can reveal adoption opportunities. Check existing tools first and preserve the form’s validation and consent; sensitive flows need manual review.
items.coverage: The report keeps blocked resources, failures, and scan limits visible. Unvisited pages, authenticated flows, and runtime-generated code can fall outside the inspected source.
items.runtime: This check remains unknown. Confirm native registration and behavior separately in a browser with WebMCP support; source findings cannot certify agent usage.

entries.shopify: Connect with Shopify OAuth to import your catalog, publish selected listing fixes and track detected AI referrals. The free onboarding scan covers up to 10 products. Ongoing listing features require activated pay-as-you-go or an active Compete, Scale or Dominate subscription; each plan’s product and simulation allowances are listed on Pricing.
entries.woocommerce: Install the free plugin to connect your catalog and offer compatible agents product search, cart quotes and checkout through your own gateway. Try up to 10 products in the free onboarding scan. Ongoing ecentic listing features require activated pay-as-you-go or an active subscription; publishing also requires read/write access. AI visit tracking is not available for WooCommerce.
entries.bigcommerce: A native BigCommerce app is on the build list. It is not available to install today, and no launch date has been promised. Explore the supported product-data formats or register your interest in the direct connection.
entries.adobe: Export your Adobe Commerce catalog to CSV and map the fields to ecentic’s supported columns before uploading. Imported records can be compared with named competitors; this route does not publish changes back to Adobe Commerce or refresh automatically.
entries.shopware: Export products from Shopware, convert the file to comma-separated CSV and map the supported columns before uploading. Update the catalog in Shopware and re-import when it changes; a direct publishing connection is still planned.
entries.wix: Bring a physical-product CSV export from Wix Stores and map it to ecentic’s supported fields. Use the imported catalog for comparisons, then apply any edits in Wix and re-import. A native Wix app is planned.
entries.prestashop: Export a product CSV from PrestaShop and map its columns before importing. ecentic saves supported product records for comparisons; this export route does not write back to your store or keep the catalog refreshed automatically.
entries.googleMerchant: For connected Shopify stores, send published listing fixes to Google Merchant Center as a supplemental data source. You connect the Merchant Center account and run the sync separately. Google’s account and product requirements still apply; this does not enroll your store in native Google checkout.
entries.productFeeds: Import a supported XML or JSON feed to save product records in ecentic. Select up to 10 products for the free onboarding scan; ongoing dashboard listing features use your activated plan. Re-import when the source changes, because scheduled feed refresh and publishing back to the feed are not available.
entries.csv: Upload comma-separated product data using the supported column names, with one product per row. Check the mapping before selecting products for a scan. The upload saves records in ecentic and leaves your source file unchanged.
entries.storeAddress: Import an accessible public Shopify or WooCommerce catalog from its store address. This gives you a read-only starting point without platform credentials. Connect the verified Shopify app or WooCommerce integration later when you need to publish changes.
entries.microsoftMerchant: A dedicated merchant-feed connection for Microsoft Copilot is planned. It is not available today. The channel page explains current requirements and the Shopify referral-tracking surface that already works.
entries.amazonShopDirect: A catalog connection for Amazon’s US Shop Direct program is on the build list. There is no ecentic connection to enable today; program availability and merchant admission remain subject to Amazon’s requirements.
entries.chatgptFeed: A dedicated ChatGPT product-feed export is planned. Today, ecentic can simulate the ChatGPT model comparing your listing with a competitor’s; a simulation does not submit your catalog to ChatGPT or enroll your store in checkout.
entries.perplexityFeed: A merchant catalog-feed connection to Perplexity is planned. It is separate from the AI-referral tracking available on connected Shopify stores and is not currently a feed you can enable in ecentic.
entries.google: Use Gemini in store simulations to compare your products with named competitors. Google Merchant Center supplemental sync is a separate Shopify connection. ecentic’s native Google checkout onboarding is still planned.
entries.chatgpt: Compare your listing with a named competitor using the ChatGPT model in a simulated shopping decision. This shows model reasoning, not live shopper traffic. A dedicated ecentic ChatGPT app and product-feed export are planned separately.
entries.claude: Include Claude in simulated comparisons between your listing and a named competitor’s. Review the fields it considered and its explanation for the choice. This is model testing inside ecentic, not a merchant-feed or checkout connection to Claude.
entries.copilot: See detected Copilot referrals on connected Shopify stores today. The Microsoft Merchant Center feed connection is still planned, so this entry does not represent a live catalog submission or checkout enrollment.
entries.perplexity: See detected Perplexity referrals on connected Shopify stores today. Perplexity store scans and a dedicated merchant feed are on the build list; neither is currently a connection you can switch on.
entries.amazon: Explore the Amazon Shop Direct route and register interest in an ecentic catalog connection. The connector is planned, with no committed launch date; Amazon determines merchant eligibility and program availability.
entries.paymentGateway: With the WooCommerce plugin, compatible agents can create an order and send the buyer to your checkout link for payment. Your WooCommerce gateway takes the payment and you remain the seller. Optional server-side Stripe payments need separate configuration.
entries.stripeAcs: A dedicated Stripe Agentic Commerce Suite connection is planned. It is separate from the optional Stripe payment flow in the WooCommerce plugin and is not available to activate as an ecentic integration today.
entries.plytix: Export product data from Plytix as CSV and map it to ecentic’s supported columns. Import the records for comparisons and re-import after changes. This is an export route, without a direct PIM connection or automatic write-back.
entries.akeneo: A direct Akeneo connection is on the build list. There is no native synchronization or write-back available in ecentic today. Register your team’s interest and describe the catalog workflow you need.
entries.salsify: A direct Salsify connection is on the build list. There is no native synchronization or write-back available in ecentic today. Register your interest to share the product-data workflow your team needs.

questions.sample: Illustrative questions; not measured search demand.

rules.models: Use ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini simulation perspectives to compare supported product facts. Perplexity currently supports Shopify referral tracking; its store simulations are coming soon. A simulation is not channel approval.

wine-and-spirits.subtitle: Make bottle facts explicit, compare the listing, and scope a purchase flow around the channel and market that permit it.
wine-and-spirits.help: Use verified origin, style, strength, price and delivery information in the comparison. Verify the source facts and permitted claims before choosing Apply, which generates and publishes the title and description. Product and destination restrictions still apply.

food-and-beverage.subtitle: Turn verified label facts into clearer product information, then review every dietary and nutrition statement before publishing.
food-and-beverage.help: Compare the ingredients, allergens, nutrition and serving information that the source actually supplies. ecentic can suggest clearer listing language; the merchant reviews claims and suitability before applying it.

beauty-and-personal-care.subtitle: Make supported ingredients and product claims easier to compare, with the evidence still attached to the source.
beauty-and-personal-care.help: Compare existing ingredients, intended use, size and supported claims. Review proposed wording against the manufacturer’s evidence; ecentic does not test efficacy or certify protection.

consumer-electronics.subtitle: Make model, compatibility and warranty information visible before a shopper reaches the store.
consumer-electronics.help: Compare the exact model and source specifications, then review suggested listing changes. Compatibility, electrical and warranty claims still need the merchant’s evidence.

home-and-furniture.subtitle: Give shoppers dimensions, materials and delivery terms they can check against their own space.
home-and-furniture.help: Compare the measurements and conditions in the source record. ecentic can expose missing listing detail; it does not guarantee fit, access or a delivery date.

fashion-and-outdoor.subtitle: Keep fit, fabric and performance descriptions tied to the product’s actual specifications.
fashion-and-outdoor.help: Compare verified sizing, materials, care and intended-use information. Review wording before publishing; ecentic does not certify technical performance or environmental claims.

health-wellness-and-pet.subtitle: Make source facts clearer without turning a product comparison into health advice.
health-wellness-and-pet.help: Compare supplied ingredients, intended use, serving or feeding information and documented standards. ecentic does not diagnose, prescribe or certify safety or health claims.

travel-and-experiences.subtitle: Make the offer’s dates, inclusions and cancellation terms explicit before the booking handoff.
travel-and-experiences.help: Compare the product information in the source. Live availability, final price and booking conditions must be confirmed with the merchant; the example is not a reservation.

bespoke.title: A custom route for age-restricted purchases.
bespoke.description: Plan an agent-assisted purchase flow with ecentic around your existing controls. Scope comes before implementation; support depends on the product, country, channel and payment provider.

steps.title: Confirm the permitted route
steps.body: Check the product, destination and chosen channel’s rules before exposing a purchase path.

steps.title: Keep the merchant’s age check
steps.body: Integrate the merchant’s existing age-verification process where required. Built-in ecentic age verification is not assumed.

steps.title: Hand over for confirmation and payment
steps.body: The buyer completes the required checks and confirms payment in the merchant’s permitted checkout flow.

reviewReplay.disclosure: A scripted sample of the facts checked and the resulting selection.

reviewSolutionsChannels.discoveryNote: Profile discovery does not establish product or checkout eligibility.
reviewSolutionsChannels.previewNote: Illustrative conversations and partial UCP responses, not live assistant answers. Product cards follow the discovery patterns documented by Google and OpenAI; ChatGPT’s commerce integration is separate from UCP.

sectors.response: Compare the verified tasting notes and bottle details.
Match the nutrition label to your serving-size and calorie limits.
Check the ingredient list and the product’s stated formulation.
Compare battery life, charging and the features you need.
Check both the closed dimensions and the space needed when open.
Compare the weather protection, measurements and return policy.
Read the ingredients and feeding guidance before comparing options.
Compare the stay details, dates and the complete booking terms.
sectors.limit: Travel availability and UCP support vary.

turns.listings: I’ll compare these two sample listings with your budget and fit requirements.
turns.fields: Both are under $400. Your listing does not state seat height or weight capacity. The rival states 44–54 cm and 120 kg.

round16Shopping.sourceHint: Present in the sample source; make it explicit in the listing.
round16Shopping.inspectionNote: Illustrative product imagery and records. This shows an evidence check, not a live recommendation or a model’s private reasoning.

round16Woo.title: Find the step that stops checkout.

round17Shopping.evidenceNote: Highlighted facts already exist in the sample source. Make them explicit in the listing before comparing again.
